solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Injury in country when crossing river

indicators.note: the country stretches across the river, so the river's letter sits inside the country

parts.note: Spain is a European country

explanation.surface: Someone hurts themselves abroad while wading across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrenched ligament in an ankle or wrist is a common kind of injury.

clue.text: Down-and-out old man given drug with heart conking out

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: the middle letter of the drug word fails and drops away, as a heart might stop

parts.note: an upper is a stimulant drug

explanation.surface: A homeless old man on drugs whose heart gives out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with heart conking out' removes the central P of UPPER, leaving UPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A down-and-out is a destitute person, someone utterly poor and living on charity.

clue.text: A truck's got fuel in for carrying rabble — they're on the road

indicators.note: the fuel goes in, placed inside the truck word

parts.note: a ute is an Australian pickup truck; 'A truck's' read as A plus UTES

indicators.note: the fuel word holds the rabble word within it

parts.note: oil is a fuel
a mob is a disorderly crowd, a rabble

explanation.surface: A lorry is refuelled while transporting an unruly crowd along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Truck' suggests a lorry, but the needed word is the Australian ute; 'truck's' gives its plural form.
explanation.definitionFit: Cars are the vehicles that travel on roads, matching the plural pronoun in the definition.

clue.text: Finally sleeping in the raw — this having been cast?

definitions.text: Finally sleeping in the raw — this having been cast?

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so the letters are scattered into a new order
the closing letter of the word sleeping is taken

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps naked because their pyjamas have been thrown off.
explanation.walkthrough: G, the last letter of 'sleeping', joins IN THE RAW and all nine letters are rearranged. The whole clue also defines: if you sleep in the raw, your pyjamas have been cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nighties are garments worn in bed, the things discarded by someone who sleeps naked.

clue.text: This writer with farewell message conveys commercial information

parts.note: the setter referring to themselves gives me

indicators.note: the goodbye word carries the advert within it

parts.note: ta-ta is an informal goodbye
an ad is a commercial, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A writer's goodbye note passes on some business news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial information' reads as one phrase, but only 'information' is the definition; 'commercial' supplies the advert.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means data describing other data, such as file tags, so it is a kind of information.

clue.text: Town offering something for mouse — jam!

parts.note: a mouse mat is the pad a computer mouse sits on
to jam is to lock, become stuck fast

explanation.surface: A mention of a computer accessory, then an exclamation about it sticking.
explanation.walkthrough: Matlock is a spa town in Derbyshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Matlock is the county town of Derbyshire, an example of a town.

clue.text: Namely, a person who is foolish to conceal love

indicators.note: the fool word hides the love letter inside it

parts.note: a twit is a silly person
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A fool who keeps their feelings hidden, as the clue goes on to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are formal phrases introducing a specification: that is to say.

clue.text: Shoe insole perhaps upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning the word upside down reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: an insole is one kind of pad, hence the 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A shoe's insole has been put in the wrong way up.
explanation.walkthrough: A dap is a regional British word, chiefly Welsh and West Country, for a plimsoll or gym shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a dialect name for a canvas sports shoe, a plimsoll.

clue.text: Union to get angry giving instruction

parts.note: TU stands for trade union
to rage is to become furious

explanation.surface: A trade union is driven to fury by an order.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching by a private tutor is a form of instruction, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Try very hard as upper class male — however kept outside

indicators.note: the conjunction is placed around the other pieces, kept on their outside

parts.note: but means however
U is the conventional label for upper class
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A posh man strives hard but is excluded anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make an enormous effort, to strain oneself.

clue.text: The thing with one foot rolling over is a wild animal

indicators.note: the combined pieces turn over, so they are read backwards

parts.note: 'the thing' can be it, as in 'you're it'
the Roman numeral for one is I
a paw is an animal's foot

explanation.surface: Something with a single foot tumbling over is an untamed beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The wapiti is a large North American deer, the elk, which lives wild.

clue.text: Pass quiet loner in the East End?

parts.note: p, piano, is the music marking for quiet

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End famously drop the H at the start of words

parts.note: a hermit is a solitary person

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a reclusive Londoner gets through unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditional working-class area of London, where Cockney speech drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass is a document granting entry or authorisation, a licence or warrant.

clue.text: Hooligan, first to last crooked, being banished

indicators.note: the opening letter of the hooligan word is shifted to its end

parts.note: a lout is a hooligan
awry means askew, crooked

explanation.surface: A thug who went bad is sent into exile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the L of LOUT to the end, making OUTL.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic noun means the state of being an outlaw, deprived of legal protection and cast out.

clue.text: Glorify a poet — he is so fantastic

indicators.note: fantastic means wild and fanciful, so the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: Someone praises a writer of verse as simply wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: To deify or exalt someone to divine status is to glorify them.

clue.text: Suggestion about king getting harsh in penetration of enemy lines

indicators.note: the suggestion word goes round the king's letter

parts.note: a breath can mean a hint or suggestion, as in a breath of scandal
K is the chess abbreviation for king
rough means harsh

explanation.surface: A hint that a monarch is becoming severe during an invasion.
explanation.definitionFit: In military terms this is the act of breaking through the opposing defences.

clue.text: Trees and barns — home on the run

indicators.note: running loose, the letters scatter into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Woodland and farm buildings near a house during a chase.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornbeam is a hardwood tree of the birch family, so the plural is trees.

clue.text: Dog show coming up could be therapeutic

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: Evita is a stage musical, a show

explanation.surface: A canine exhibition on the way might be good for one's health.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with healing power is therapeutic; the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: All surf there when this clay is dissolved?

indicators.note: dissolving breaks up the letters so they re-form in another order

explanation.surface: Waves wash away a beach made of this soft clay.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an absorbent clay once used to clean wool, so it is a type of clay.

clue.text: Not first in race — most of the spectators suffer humiliation

indicators.note: the opening letter of the race word is removed

parts.note: a heat is a qualifying race

indicators.note: all but the final letter of the spectators word is used

parts.note: a crowd is a gathering of spectators

explanation.surface: Not winning a race in front of the fans is humiliating.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to admit one was wrong and be humbled.

clue.text: Something prickly left under rag

indicators.note: in a down clue the left letter sits beneath the rag word

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A thorny thing is left beneath a scrap of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The teasel is a plant with spiny flower heads, so it is a prickly thing.

clue.text: Scoundrel holding the woman in gym is exposed in police account

indicators.note: the scoundrel word grips the rest inside it

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel

indicators.note: the woman goes inside the gym letters

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A villain grabs a woman in the gym, and the police report reveals it.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal record kept by the police is an account of a person's offences.

clue.text: Nuclear physicist, heading off for a stiff climb

indicators.note: the physicist's surname loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: Hans Geiger was the German physicist of the radiation counter

explanation.surface: A scientist sets off for a hard mountain ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: This Swiss Alpine peak, with its notorious north face, is a famously demanding climb.

clue.text: Big Aussie thug, the first person to be caught

indicators.note: the first person is captured inside the thug word

parts.note: a boor is a rough, uncouth person
the first person pronoun is me

explanation.surface: A large Australian ruffian is the first to be arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia the word is slang for a large male kangaroo, a big Aussie animal.

clue.text: Car feature's special bargain, reduced slightly

definitions.note: read as 'car feature is', the 's joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: special here means made specially, so the letters are reworked
a small cut takes off the final letter

explanation.surface: A car's extra is on special offer at a small discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced slightly' cuts the final N from BARGAIN, and 'special' rearranges BARGAI.
explanation.definitionFit: This inflating safety cushion is fitted in a vehicle's steering wheel or dashboard.

clue.text: Cricketer: lure getting one out

indicators.note: out signals that the letter for one is removed from the lure word

parts.note: bait is a lure
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A cricketer is tempted into getting a batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the word is short for batsman, one kind of cricketer.

clue.text: Most willing to offer cash ahead of time

indicators.note: the cash word comes before the time letter

parts.note: readies is British slang for ready cash

explanation.surface: The keenest person offers to pay up early.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready can mean willing, so the superlative means the most willing.

clue.text: Agreement to save pounds with project creating a bit of a stir?

indicators.note: save means except, so the pounds letter is left out

parts.note: a deal is an agreement
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling
to project is to throw

explanation.surface: A deal that avoids costs and plans to cause a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' is slang for prison, so 'a bit of a stir' is a section of a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The cell block holding condemned prisoners is one part of a prison, stir being slang for jail.

clue.text: Magic periods of limited duration?

definitions.meaning: a wizard's incantations, charms and enchantments
short stretches of time, such as a cold snap

explanation.surface: Wizardry described as only temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both magic charms and short stretches of time.
